items.note: Online art platform data compare AI-assisted creators with matched non-adopters on novel artifact contributions (productivity and dilution effects, Stable Diffusion release); Science Advances version, an SSRN version also exists.

Within-subject experiment: 96 university students do a scientific divergent application task under group-AI, individual-AI, and human-only group modes, with outputs scored for usefulness, originality, and quality; the abstract does not say whether the order of modes was randomized.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, ScienceDirect, web search); the title suggests a follow-up of music students after ChatGPT-4 use on creative and analytical skills (possible after_ai), so the full text must show whether there is a comparison group and scored creative output.
Platform data on over 4 million artworks from more than 50,000 users track productivity, favorites, and content and visual novelty before and after text-to-image AI adoption; no assignment of AI.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, SSRN page blocked, web search); the title says experimental evidence on generative AI adoption in creative tasks, Holzner et al. 2025 code the SSRN version (10.2139/ssrn.5196748) as people with versus without AI; JEBO 2026 version.

Abstract not reachable and no DOI found; per the search notes, alternate uses task responses from student dyads are compared with responses from 10 generative AI models and no participant used AI (CHI EA 2024 TREW workshop paper).

GPT-4 product ideas are rated against ideas from laypeople and incentivized creative professionals, and GPT-4 rewrites of human ideas are rated; no participant works with AI; related to Li, Castelo, Katona and Sarvary (Marketing Science) per the search notes.

Compares 20 AI systems with 193 university students on the PIC-A creative imagination test, and adds a quasi-experimental pre/post phase in which students repeat the games with ChatGPT help, scoring fluency, flexibility, and narrative originality; no randomized order or control group is stated.
Several LLMs and human writers write the same story prompt, and human raters score fluency, coherence, originality, humor, and style; no participant uses AI; arXiv 2310.08433 is the same work.
ChatGPT-4 and humans give creative interpretations of ambiguous figures (Figural Interpretation Quest), scored for flexibility and rated creativity; no participant uses AI.
